stem: Ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, is manufactured from nitrogen and hydrogen by the Haber process. $$\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H = -92\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Some bond energies are given.

$\text{N}\equiv\text{N} = 944\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\text{H}-\text{H} = 436\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain the meaning of the term bond energy.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the data to calculate a value for the N-H bond energy.
**You must show your working.**

parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text: Using the same axes, sketch a second curve to indicate the Boltzmann distribution at a higher temperature.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: **With reference to the Boltzmann distribution**, state and explain the effect of increasing temperature on the rate of production of ammonia.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State and explain the effect of increasing temperature on the yield of ammonia. Use Le Chatelier's principle to explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: At a pressure of $2.00 \times 10^7\text{ Pa}$, $1.00\text{ mol}$ of nitrogen, $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$, was mixed with $3.00\text{ mol}$ of hydrogen, $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$. The final equilibrium mixture formed contained $0.300\text{ mol}$ of ammonia, $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the amounts, in mol, of $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ in the equilibrium mixture.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the partial pressure of ammonia, $p_{\text{NH}_3}$, in the equilibrium mixture.

Give your answer to **three** significant figures.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
In another equilibrium mixture the partial pressures are as shown.

| substance | partial pressure / Pa |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ | $2.20 \times 10^6$ |
| $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ | $9.62 \times 10^5$ |
| $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ | $1.40 \times 10^4$ |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Write the expression for the equilibrium constant, $K_{\text{p}}$, for the production of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the value of $K_{\text{p}}$ for this reaction.

State the units.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
This reaction is repeated with the same starting amounts of nitrogen and hydrogen. The same temperature is used but the container has a smaller volume.

State the effects, if any, of this change on the yield of ammonia and on the value of $K_{\text{p}}$.
